Assume Full Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching shape-regular affine triangulation in two dimensions, let each cell $K$ have an arbitrary finite total degree $p_K\ge1$, and let $u\in C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $u|_K\in H^2(K)$ for every cell. For every edge $E$, let $\tau_E$ be either unit tangent direction and write $\partial_{\tau_E}v=\nabla v\cdot\tau_E$. For an interior edge $E=K\cap K'$, set $p_E=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; for a boundary edge of $K$, set $p_E=p_K$. Put $m_K=\min_{E\subset\partial K}p_E$. There is a linear interpolant $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$ in the trace-matching space of [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]]. It preserves any zero boundary edge data: if $u$ vanishes on a boundary edge, so does $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$. For every $q\in\mathbb P_{m_K}(K;\mathbb R)$,

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le |u-q|_{H^1(K)}+C_\gamma\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right),
$$

and

$$
h_K^{-1}\|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)} \le C_\gamma\left(h_K^{-1}\|u-q\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-q|_{H^1(K)}+\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right)\right).
$$

The constant is independent of the degrees and their ratios. In particular, if integer $r\ge5$, $m_K\ge2r-4$, $n_K=\lfloor m_K/2\rfloor$, and $u|_K\in H^r(K)$, then

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le C_{r,\gamma}h_K^{r-1}\left(\frac{(n_K-r+3)!}{(n_K+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$

For $m_K\ge4(r-2)$ the factorial factor is at most $(4/m_K)^{r-4}$. The effective degree $m_K$ records the lowest degree among the shared edge traces; no rate independent of neighboring trace degrees is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ x+y<1\}$, let $r\ge5$ be an integer, let $p\ge2r-4$ be an integer, and put $n=\lfloor p/2\rfloor$ and

$$
\eta_{n,r}=\left(\frac{(n-r+3)!}{(n+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}.
$$

There is a bounded linear map $A_{p,r}:H^r(T;\mathbb R)\to\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$, where $\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$ is the restriction of real polynomials in $(x,y)$ of total degree at most $p$. It is explicitly defined in the proof from the reference-simplex extension, a unique moment polynomial, and finite Legendre projections, and satisfies

$$
\|u-A_{p,r}u\|_{H^2(T)}\le C_r\eta_{n,r}|u|_{H^r(T)}.
$$

Here $C_r$ is independent of $p$ and is the product of a fixed reference extension bound, the reference moment-projection bound, and an absolute tensor-projection constant; no useful growth bound in $r$ is asserted. For a shape-regular affine triangle $K$ of diameter $h_K$, affine transport gives

$$
\left(\sum_{j=0}^2h_K^{2j-2}|u-A_{K,p,r}u|_{H^j(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_{r,\gamma}\eta_{n,r}h_K^{r-1}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$

If $p\ge4(r-2)$, then $\eta_{n,r}\le(4/p)^{r-4}$. This is a conservative ordinary Sobolev rate; it is neither an optimal $p^{-(r-1)}$ estimate nor an analytic growth estimate for $C_r$.

Assume Countable Choice. On a finite matching affine simplicial mesh or a finite face-to-face affine tensor-box mesh, a piecewise polynomial scalar function whose two traces agree on every interior facet belongs to $H^1(\Omega)$, and its weak gradient equals its ordinary cellwise polynomial gradient almost everywhere. The simplex degrees may vary by cell; the box degrees may also vary.

Let $d\ge2$ and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ in the sense of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. A **degree map** is a function $p:\mathcal T\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite values. The broken simplex space associated with $(\mathcal T,p)$ is
$$
V^{\mathrm{br}}(\mathcal T,p):=\{v\in L^2(\Omega):v|_K\in\mathbb P_{p_K}(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T\},
$$
where $p_K:=p(K)$ and $\mathbb P_m(K)$ denotes restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $m$. Its **conforming hp space** is the subspace of functions whose two polynomial traces agree on every interior facet. The zero-boundary hp space further requires the polynomial trace to vanish on every boundary facet. For an interior facet $F=K\cap K'$, its trace degree is $p_F:=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; equality of the two traces means that their common polynomial belongs to $\mathbb P_{p_F}(F)$.

A **matching affine tensor-box mesh** is a finite face-to-face partition of a bounded polytope into affine images of $[-1,1]^d$, with pairwise disjoint interiors. For a scalar degree $p_K$ on each box, the local tensor space is $\mathbb Q_{p_K}(K)$, the pullback of polynomials of degree at most $p_K$ in each reference coordinate. The conforming box hp space is defined by equality of polynomial traces across every shared face, and its zero-boundary subspace by zero traces on the exterior faces. For a shared face $F=K\cap K'$, set $p_F=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; its common trace lies in $\mathbb Q_{p_F}(F)$ in tangential reference coordinates. This definition of tensor boxes does not include curved or non-affine cells.

On either mesh, **h-refinement** replaces one cell by a finite matching partition of that cell and assigns degrees to the children; **p-refinement** raises at least one cell degree while leaving the mesh fixed; **hp-refinement** performs both operations. A local polynomial basis is **hierarchical** if its ordered degree layers span the nested spaces $\mathbb P_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb P_p$ (or $\mathbb Q_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb Q_p$), with each new layer extending the preceding span. For example, pullbacks of reference monomials $\widehat x^\nu$ ordered by $|\nu|$ give such a basis for $\mathbb P_p$, and tensor monomials $\xi^\nu$ ordered by $\max_i\nu_i$ give one for $\mathbb Q_p$. This basis convention does not assert stability of a particular basis or projector.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in its first argument, conjugate-linear
in its second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad \operatorname{Re}a(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2.$$
Let $F:V\to\mathbb K$ be bounded and conjugate-linear, and let $V_h\subseteq V$
be finite-dimensional. Then there are unique $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ with
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V).$$
$$a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h).$$
The solutions satisfy
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac M\alpha\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
The real bilinear case uses linear functionals and reads $\operatorname{Re}$ as
the identity.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, used to invoke the published real and complex
$L^p$ completeness results through their Countable-Choice interface. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p\le\infty$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, equipped with the displayed norm of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], is a complete normed space over
$\mathbb K$.

Both endpoints $p=1$ and $p=\infty$ are included, as is $k=0$, where the
assertion reduces to the completeness of $L^p$. If $\Omega=\varnothing$, then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is the zero space and the assertion is trivial.
The Axiom of Choice is used only to derive Countable Choice for the two
published completeness interfaces; no other selection is made. Representative
selection inside the finitely many coordinate classes is finite and
choice-free.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1\le p<\infty$, integer $r\ge1$,
integer $s\ge0$, and real-valued $v\in W^{\max(r,s),p}(\widehat S_d)$.
There is a polynomial $q\in\mathbb P_{r-1}(\widehat S_d)$, chosen by
matching all means $\int_{\widehat S_d}D^\alpha q=
\int_{\widehat S_d}D^\alpha v$ for $|\alpha|\le r-1$, such that:

- if $0\le s\le r$, then
  $\|v-q\|_{W^{s,p}(\widehat S_d)}\le C|v|_{W^{r,p}(\widehat S_d)}$;
- if $s>r$, then
  $\|v-q\|_{W^{s,p}(\widehat S_d)}\le
  C\sum_{j=r}^{s}|v|_{W^{j,p}(\widehat S_d)}$.

The second clause assumes $v\in W^{s,p}$; constants depend only on
$d,p,r,s$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching
affine simplicial mesh, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $v$ be a real-valued
conforming piecewise polynomial whose polynomial trace vanishes on every boundary
facet. Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Here $W^{1,p}_0$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no C1
trace characterization is used.

derivations.claim: Both norm branches are Hilbert: the Sobolev inner product is complete by [F4], the zero-boundary Sobolev closure is closed, and Poincaré makes its gradient norm equivalent to the inherited complete norm. The finite matching polynomial space is finite-dimensional and conforming by [F3]. The given exact form and load therefore meet Céa's precise hypotheses, giving unique variational solutions and $\|u-u_{\mathcal T,p}\|_V\le(M_a/\alpha_a)\inf_{v\in V_{\mathcal T,p}}\|u-v\|_V$.

The interpolant [F1] belongs to the trace-matching space. In the zero-boundary branch, [F1] also gives zero polynomial traces on every boundary facet. Apply [F6] with exponent $2$ to obtain $Iu\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, so the interpolant is an admissible comparison in either norm branch. No neighboring degree ratio was used.

Sum the squared cell seminorm bounds in [F1], which gives $|u-Iu|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2\le C_\gamma^2\sum_KJ_K(q_K)^2$ by [F3]. The full scaled estimate also gives $\|u-Iu\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\le C_\gamma^2\sum_Kh_K^2R_K(q_K)^2$. Their sum with the exact factor $\chi$ bounds $\|u-Iu\|_V^2$. Use $Iu$ as the admissible comparison in step 1.1 and take square roots to obtain the first displayed Galerkin bound. The local comparisons may be chosen independently because the single interpolant was constructed from common edge traces of $u$, rather than by gluing the $q_K$.

Choose the reference moment polynomial of degree $s_K-1$ from [F5] and transport it to $K$. The degree condition makes it an admissible $q_K\in\mathbb P_{m_K}(K)$. With $w_K=u-q_K$, scaling gives $h_K^{-1}\|w_K\|_2+|w_K|_{H^1}+h_K|w_K|_{H^2}\le C_{s_K,\gamma}h_K^{s_K-1}|u|_{H^{s_K}(K)}$. The value and derivative edge trace bounds proved in [F1] therefore give the same bound for $J_K$ and $R_K$. Substitute into step 2.1 to prove the general integer-regularity h estimate, including $s_K=2$ on every degree assignment.

Under the stronger cellwise assumptions choose $q_K$ from [F2]. The scaled edge trace proved in [F1] gives $J_K(q_K),R_K(q_K)\le C_{r_K,\gamma}h_K^{r_K-1}\eta_K|u|_{H^{r_K}(K)}$: its value-edge term is bounded by $C(h_K^{-1}\|w_K\|_2+|w_K|_{H^1})$, and its derivative-edge term by $C(|w_K|_{H^1}+h_K|w_K|_{H^2})$, so exactly the three scaled norms in [F2] occur. Substitution into step 2.1 proves the second displayed bound with $(1+\chi h_K^2)$. Finally [F2] gives $\eta_K\le(4/m_K)^{r_K-4}$ under the stronger degree threshold. This retains the actual trace-degree and regularity constants and concludes both norm branches.
